'''Pablo Augusto Ferrari''' (September 11, 1949) is an Argentine mathematician, member of the [[Bernoulli Society]], the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]], and the [[International Statistical Institute]]. He is also co-principal investigator at the Brazilian research center [[NeuroMat]].<ref>[http://neuromat.numec.prp.usp.br/team NeuroMat Team]</ref> Ferrari investigates probabilistic models of microscopic phenomena and macroscopic counterpart. He is the son of the contemporary conceptual artist [[León Ferrari]].

== Biography ==
Pablo Ferrari was born in 1949 in [[Buenos Aires]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-09-01 |title=Galeria de Diretores: Pablo Augusto Ferrari |url=https://www.ime.usp.br/historia/galeria-de-diretores-e-vice-diretores/pablo-augusto-ferrari/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=IME-USP |language=pt-BR}}</ref> He is the son of the contemporary conceptual artist [[León Ferrari]] with Alicia Barros Castro and has two sisters: Marialí and Ariel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=León Ferrari |url=https://leonferrari.com.ar/bio/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=leonferrari.com.ar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=SP-Arte |url=https://www.sp-arte.com/editorial/leon-ferrari-arte-e-imaginario-familiar |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=www.sp-arte.com}}</ref>

He got a degree in mathematics from the [[University of Buenos Aires]] (UBA) in 1974, PhD in Statistics from the [[University of Sao Paulo]] (USP) in 1982, with the dissertation  ''Invariant measures for the marked simple exclusion process'', advised by Enrique Daniel Andjel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pablo Ferrari - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=47805 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250514104705/https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=47805 |archive-date=2025-05-14 |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org |url-status=live }}</ref> He also has a postdoctoral from [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]].<ref name=":0" />

Ferrari was Professor at the USP from 1978 to 2008 and was the vice Dean of the [[Institute of Mathematics and Statistics, University of São Paulo|Institute of Mathematics and Statistics]] twice, one from 1994 to 1998 and the other from 1998 to 2002.<ref name=":0" />

He was a visiting professor at Rutgers, Paris, Rome, Santiago de Chile and Cambridge. He is a UBA Professor and Researcher of CONICET from 2009 and a member of the Group Probability of Buenos Aires. He received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1999, the [[Consecration Award]] of the Academy of Exact, Physical and Natural Sciences in Buenos Aires in 2011 and was named a fellow of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Factory |first=Troop Software |title=Pablo Augusto Ferrari {{!}} Fundación Konex |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=www.fundacionkonex.org |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pablo Augusto Ferrari – ABC – Academia Brasileira de Ciências |url=https://www.abc.org.br/membro/pablo-augusto-ferrari/ |access-date=2025-07-03 |website=www.abc.org.br}}</ref> Also, he is a honored member of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematical Statistics {{!}} Pablo Ferrari: Doob Lecture |url=https://imstat.org/2024/05/15/pablo-ferrari-doob-lecture/ |access-date=2025-07-07 |language=en}}</ref>
